question.worked_solution:
From the definition of $f(x),$ the left-sided limit of $f(x)$ at $x=-2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -{2}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to -{2}^{-}}\frac{{x}^{2}-5x-14}{x+2} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -{2}^{-}}\frac{(x-7)(x+2)}{x+2} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -{2}^{-}}\frac{(x-7)\cancel{(x+2)}}{\cancel{x+2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -{2}^{-}}(x-7) \\  & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -{2}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to -{2}^{+}}({k}^{1-x}-10) \\  & ={k}^{1-(-2)}-10 \\  & ={k}^{3}-10.\end{aligned}
$$

We also note that $f(-2)={k}^{3}-10$ 

So, for $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x=-2,$ we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -{2}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to -{2}^{-}}f(x) \\ {k}^{3}-10 & =-9 \\ {k}^{3} & =1 \\ k & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, for the function to be continuous at $x=-2,$ we need $k=1.$
